candidates: When generating unique variable name suffixes from file paths in codegen utilities (e.g., `codegen-project-annotations.ts`), use a distribution-stable hash algorithm such as djb2 or FNV-1a rather than a sum-of-char-codes approach. Summing char codes produces identical values for any permutation of the same characters (e.g., 'abc' and 'cba'), causing silent variable-name collisions.

When a Vite plugin's `config` hook needs to append to `envPrefix`, always read the current value, normalize it to an array, and deduplicate with the new prefix—never replace the existing value outright. Replacing it silently drops all user-configured env-var prefixes.

Never wrap the generic parameter of `presets.apply<T>()` in `Promise<>`. The method already returns `Promise<T>`, so `presets.apply<Promise<SomeType>>('key')` produces a double-Promise; after a single `await` the variable is still a Promise, breaking every downstream consumer (e.g., `Object.keys(envs)` or `stringifyProcessEnvs(envs, ...)`). Use `presets.apply<SomeType>('key')` instead.

JSDoc comments on preset functions (e.g., `viteCorePlugins`, `viteFinal`) must list only the plugins the function actually returns. After any refactor that moves responsibilities between functions, audit the JSDoc to remove references to plugins that are now added elsewhere (e.g., in `vite-config.ts` or `vitest-plugin/index.ts`) so the documentation does not mislead future readers.

When building a value with conditional logic—such as constructing an `externals` map that conditionally adds an entry when a feature flag like `disableBlocks` is enabled—verify that the final computed value is explicitly passed to every function that needs it. A computed-but-never-forwarded value means the conditional branch is silently dead.

Remove unused parameters from exported function signatures. A parameter that is never referenced in the body (e.g., the `existing: PluginOption[]` parameter of `viteCorePlugins`) and is always called with a placeholder like `[]` is dead code that misleads callers about the function's contract.

In a Vite plugin's `config` hook, when contributing to `optimizeDeps.entries`, read and normalize the user's existing entries to an array and merge with plugin-provided paths—never unconditionally replace the field. Replacing it disables Vite's default HTML-file entry inference and silently drops any explicit entries the user or other plugins have already set.

In builder-vite's codegen utilities, import statements embedded in *generated source code* must use the public virtual module ID (e.g., `virtual:/@storybook/builder-vite/project-annotations.js`). The `\0`-prefixed resolved ID returned by `getResolvedVirtualModuleId` is an internal Vite plugin-system convention for use only inside `resolveId` and `load` hooks, never in emitted JavaScript.

When refactoring environment-variable injection from an ad-hoc location (e.g., `sanitizeEnvVars`) into a shared Vite plugin added via `viteCorePlugins`, confirm that the plugin is applied in *every* consumer—including `@storybook/addon-vitest`'s plugin stack—so the refactor does not silently drop `process.env.*` substitution in Vitest test runs.

When extracting `getProjectAnnotations` logic into a new virtual module (e.g., `project-annotations.js`), the `import.meta.hot.accept(...)` handler that calls `window.__STORYBOOK_PREVIEW__.onGetProjectAnnotationsChanged` must be defined in that same virtual module, not left in the caller. Moving the logic without moving its HMR boundary breaks live-reload for project annotations.

After refactoring logic out of a module (e.g., moving `composeConfigs` composition into `codegen-project-annotations.ts`), remove any imports in the original file that are no longer referenced. Stale imports in codegen files (`codegen-modern-iframe-script.ts`, etc.) are noise and can confuse future readers about what the file depends on.

When assembling a Vite plugin array in `pluginConfig` (builder-vite's `vite-config.ts`), explicitly verify that the relative ordering of transform plugins is intentional. In particular, confirm whether `enforce: 'post'` plugins such as `injectExportOrderPlugin` should run before or after other transform plugins like `csfPlugin`, since the insertion position in the array determines execution order for same-phase plugins.
